content:
If you've been testing Apple Watch beta apps all summer, you may have noticed some existing apps won't open on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is automatically updating these apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The updates will be pushed through the App Store, with release notes stating: 'This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27, and no new features were added.'

Apple notified developers this week that the entire update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems, is expected to officially launch to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates are being completed just in time before the release.

Apple explained that because some watchOS apps are experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture, this measure is necessary. Reports indicate Apple is automatically reprocessing and repackaging affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning properly without requiring additional action from developers.
